recipe_version.title: Ivorian Chicken Kedjenou with Eggplant, Tomatoes, and Rice
recipe_version.description: Bone-in chicken thighs layered in a sealed Dutch oven with onion, tomatoes, eggplant, red bell pepper, a whole Scotch bonnet, garlic, ginger, thyme, and bay, gently stewed in their own juices without added liquid, served over long-grain rice.

ingredients.name: bone-in skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.display_name: bone-in skinless chicken thighs (8, about 5 oz each)

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet
ingredients.display_name: Scotch bonnet chile, left whole and pricked once

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Season the chicken with 1 3/4 tsp salt. Slice the onion and bell pepper, chop the tomatoes, cube the eggplant, mince the garlic, grate the ginger, prick the Scotch bonnet once, and rinse the rice.

steps.title: Seal and stew
steps.body: Rub the oil over the bottom of the 5.5-quart Dutch oven. Layer half the onion, 4 thighs, half the vegetables, garlic, and ginger, then the remaining thighs and vegetables, the Scotch bonnet, thyme, and bay leaves. Cover tightly and cook over medium-low without adding liquid. Four or five times during cooking, hold the lid down with oven mitts and shake the pot instead of stirring. Cook until the chicken is 175 F at the bone and the vegetables collapse, about 50 minutes. Discard the chile, thyme stems, and bay leaves.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.body: During the stew (overlap stated): combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/4 tsp salt in the lidded 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, cover, turn to low, and cook 15 minutes. Rest covered off the heat 10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Spoon rice into bowls and ladle the chicken and thick vegetable stew over it.

coverage_contribution: West African dishes in the catalog are maafe, jollof, and egusi-style stews; there is no Ivorian dish and no liquid-free sealed-pot stew. A hands-off poultry dinner.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with malian-chicken-maafe: a tomato-vegetable stew cooked in its own juices, not a peanut-butter sauce. Compared with puerto-rican-pollo-guisado: Scotch bonnet, ginger, and eggplant with no sofrito, olives, or potatoes. Compared with italian-chicken-cacciatore: a West African chile-ginger stew over rice, not a wine-tomato braise with mushrooms.
not_duplicate_of: Not jollof (rice is served on the side) and not a peanut stew.
